text:
rebecca_support: Hey all — AcmeCorp reporting streaming responses are cut off after long idle (~5-10m). Clients reconnect aggressively and they saw a billing spike. Happens behind Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx. Partial chunks returned, then client gets 502 on reconnect. Any ideas?

zack_sre: Can you paste a minimal repro curl and the raw headers from the origin responses? Also what are ALB idle timeout and CF timeout values?

rebecca_support: Repro curl we used: 
```
curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood-prod.example/v1/stream' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
```
Output shows SSE stream for ~6m, then a silent gap, then a truncated chunk and immediate 502 on the next connect. Example chunk log (timestamps are client-side):
```
[00:00:00] :event: token
[00:00:00] data: {"t":1}
...
[00:05:53] :heartbeat
[00:05:53] data: :keepalive
[00:11:05] <no data for 120s>
[00:11:07] HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

ingrid_oncall: That gap looks like an upstream close somewhere. Cloudflare commonly has a ~100s idle timeout between CF and origin for some plans, ALB defaults to 60s unless changed. Double proxy situation -> if any layer closes silently, client sees truncated stream and then reconnects. Also CF can buffer small writes when using HTTP/1.1, resulting in apparent pauses.

sam_dev: Couple quick mitigations: send a lightweight SSE comment ping every 15-25s from the app to ensure bytes flow. Make sure the app sets `Connection: keep-alive` and uses chunked transfer encoding. On nginx, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_send_timeout 300s; proxy_read_timeout 300s;` so nginx doesn't batch or drop the stream.

rebecca_support: Customer already had `proxy_read_timeout` at 60s, I asked them to bump to 400s. They said Cloudflare still cut after ~100s.

cf-bot: Cloudflare note: connection between Cloudflare and origin may be closed after ~100s of inactivity on some edge tiers. Consider enabling "Origin Keepalive" and ensure origin sends periodic bytes. Also disabling HTTP/2 between CF and origin sometimes reduces buffering.

zack_sre: Another angle: ALB has an idle timeout setting at the target group level — bump that to > origin keepalive. If using NLB, connections are TCP and usually keepalive needs kernel tweak. For Envoy fronting the app, check `connection_idle_timeout` settings.

alex_customer: We saw the token billing spike because our client retried immediately 10x when connection dropped. We don't have a jitter/backoff in the reconnect logic. Any best practice?

sam_dev: Add exponential backoff with jitter on reconnects. Also use `Last-Event-ID`/recover semantics where possible so server can resume instead of re-streaming expensive work. If you can't resume, limit retries client-side to avoid runaway token usage.

rebecca_support: For repro, I gave them a tiny nc-based server we used to simulate:
```
# simulate SSE server that sends a heartbeat every 20s
while true; do printf 'data: hi\n\n'; sleep 20; done | nc -l 8080
```
They could reproduce the close behaviour when inserting a 120s sleep.

ingrid_oncall: Ops checklist we ran through with them:
- ensure app emits keepalive comment every 15s
- nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_send_timeout 360s; proxy_read_timeout 360s; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`
- ALB: idle timeout -> 400s
- Cloudflare: enable origin keepalive / reduce buffering, or use a Workers edge to proxy SSE (Workers can stream)
- client: implement jittered exponential backoff + Last-Event-ID handling

zack_sre: Also checked logs: origin had no error, upstream (ALB) closed connection with `RST` at 00:11:05 — that's consistent with an idle timeout at some intermediate layer. We flagged CF Support to confirm the exact edge timeout for the customer's zone (ticket #CF-2219).

rebecca_support: Customer applied nginx changes and added server-side pings. They increased ALB idle timeout. CF Support replied: origin side closed after 105s when no bytes were sent; recommended enabling frequent keepalives. After changes the stream stayed up for >30m in our test.

alex_customer: Confirmed reduced reconnects and token usage. Billing spike was partly offset after we added client backoff too — thanks!

rebecca_support: Marking this resolved for now. Will follow up if CF ticket indicates a different fix. Saving notes to KB: "SSE behind Cloudflare+ALB: ensure periodic bytes, disable proxy buffering, increase ALB idle timeout, implement client backoff and Last-Event-ID." :white_check_mark:
